title: Find out who changed what, and why

scenario.brief:
**Where you are.** Priya has been helping with `my-notes`. The recipe now says the oven should be at 220 degrees. You remember writing 180. Who changed it, and why? History knows.

**Three ways to read history.**

- `git log --oneline` lists every commit: short id and headline.
- `git blame recipe.md` shows, for every line in the file, which commit last changed it and who made it.
- `git show <id>` shows one commit in full: author, message, and the exact lines changed. Use the short id from blame or log.

**What you'll do.** Open `ANSWERS.md` and fill in the three lines. Every answer is in the history, not in your memory.

1. The short id of the commit that changed the temperature to 220.
2. The name of the person who made it.
3. The reason given in that commit's message.

Then save your answers to history: `git add ANSWERS.md` and commit.
scenario.whyItMatters: Every engineer spends time asking "why is this line here?". Blame and show turn that question into a thirty-second lookup instead of a guess.

Bake: 40 minutes

Commit id:

objectives.title: Write the short commit id on the "Commit id" line
hints: Several commits touched recipe.md. You need the one that changed the oven line, not the latest one.
`git blame recipe.md` prints each line with the id of the commit that last changed it. Look at the "Oven" line.
Run `git blame recipe.md`, copy the id at the start of the Oven line, open `ANSWERS.md` in the editor and paste it after "Commit id:". Save with Ctrl+S.

objectives.title: Write who made the change on the "Changed by" line
hints: Blame shows a name next to each line too.
`git show <id>` prints the Author line at the top.
Write `Changed by: Priya Natarajan` in ANSWERS.md.

objectives.title: Write the reason from the commit message on the "Reason" line
hints: The headline only says what changed. The reason is in the body of the message.
`git show <id>` prints the full message, body included.
Write something like `Reason: 220 degrees gives a crisp crust; 180 came out pale and soft.`

objectives.title: Commit your answers
hints: Same loop as always: add, commit.
`git add ANSWERS.md` then `git commit -m "Answer the oven temperature question"`.
Type: `git add ANSWERS.md` and then `git commit -m "Answer the oven temperature question"`

debrief.summary: You traced a change to the commit, the person and the reason behind it, using nothing but history.
internals: `git blame` looks at the file's history commit by commit and, for each current line, finds the most recent commit that changed it.
`git show` prints a commit object: author, date, message, and the lines added and removed compared with the commit before it.
Short ids are the first seven characters of the full id. Git accepts them as long as they are unique in the repository.

keyCommands.note: Which commit last touched each line.
Only commits that changed one file.

commonMistakes: Assuming the newest commit made the change you care about.
Reading only the headline and missing the reason in the body.
debrief.atWork: On real teams, blame plus the commit message plus the linked ticket is how you understand code written by people who have since left.
debrief.interview: "How would you find out why a line of code exists?" Answer: git blame on the line, then git show on that commit.

solution:
echo -e "# Who changed the oven temperature?

Commit id: {{label:temp:short}}
Changed by: Priya Natarajan
Reason: 220 degrees gives a crisp crust; 180 came out pale and soft." > ANSWERS.md
git commit -m "Answer the oven temperature question"
